title: langgraph server Interrupts
body:
I've implemented interrupts in my Python langgraph workflow expecting them to render the ThreadView component, similar to what was demonstrated in your YouTube video. However, I'm unable to see the human input as shown in the video. My code is currently hosted on a langgraph server. Can you help me identify what might be causing this issue?


`def redact_pdf_document(gs_url:str ,config: Optional[List[str]] = None):
    """
    Redacts personally identifiable information (PII) from a PDF document.
    
    This function applies redaction to sensitive 
    information based on the specified configuration. If no configuration is provided,
    default redaction is applied to all common PII types.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    gs_url : str
        Google Storage URL pointing to the PDF document to be processed.
    
    config : List, optional
        List of specific PII types to redact. If None, all common PII types are redacted.
        Available PII types include:
        - EMAIL_ADDRESS: Email addresses
        - PHONE_NUMBER: Phone numbers in various formats
        - CREDIT_CARD_NUMBER: Credit card numbers
        - SSN: Social Security Numbers
    
    Returns:
    --------
    dict
        A dictionary containing:
        - 'redacted_url': Google Storage URL to the redacted document
        - 'status': Success or failure status of the operation
    
    Examples:
    ---------
    >>> redact_pdf_document("gs://my-bucket/sensitive-doc.pdf", ["EMAIL_ADDRESS", "PHONE_NUMBER", "SSN"])
    """
    base_url = f'{BACKEND_URL}/pii-redaction'
    print('testing logs')
    # URL encode the gs_url parameter
    encoded_gs_url = urllib.parse.quote(gs_url)
    
    # Full endpoint URL with query parameter
    endpoint = f'{base_url}?gs_url={encoded_gs_url}'
    print('redacting document ', gs_url)
  
    request = HumanInterrupt(
        action_request=ActionRequest(
            action="run_command",  # The action being requested
            args={"command": "ls", "args": ["-l"]}  # Arguments for the action
        ),
        config=HumanInterruptConfig(
            allow_ignore=True,    # Allow skipping this step
            allow_respond=True,   # Allow text feedback
            allow_edit=False,     # Don't allow editing
            allow_accept=True     # Allow direct acceptance
        ),
        description="Please review the command before execution"
    )
    # Send the interrupt request and get the response
    # Make the POST request
    response = requests.post(
        endpoint,
        headers={'accept': 'application/json'},
        data=''  # Empty data as shown in the example
    )
    response = interrupt([request])[0]
    print('human response===>',response)
    # Check if the request was successful
    if response.status_code == 200:
        result = response.json()
        result['status'] = 'success'
        return result
    else:
        return {
            "redacted_url": "",
            "status": f"failed with status code: {response.status_code}, message: {response.text}"
        }
     `
I'm implementing the code above as a tool in my workflow. Would you also be able to share the email agent langgraph code that was demonstrated in the video you referenced? That would be very helpful for my implementation
author: syedfakher27

comments.body: I would really appreciate a solution to this also. Thank you

Interrupts can't work properly with an async UI due to the nature of the HTTP protocol.

My solution:

1. Use a supervisor and a multi-agent system.
2. Replace interrupt with Command(goto=END, update=dict(current_agent='xxx')).
3. Switch execution to the current agent on START.

So bascially the issue was that I was using tool directly bind with the llm like this 
`query_check = query_check_prompt | llm.bind_tools(
    [db_query_tool], tool_choice="required"
)`
when you bind your tool like this then your tool is not considered as a separate langgraph node and you always hit the interrupt inside a langgraph node. So I changed my code like this to make the tool as an independent node

`
from langgraph.prebuilt import ToolNode
from react_agent.tools import TOOLS

model = load_chat_model(configuration.model).bind_tools(TOOLS)
builder.add_node("tools", ToolNode(TOOLS))
`
Now the langgraph will treat your TOOLS as separate node
